rules.requiredOutcome: Every retained schema migrates atomically to the current editable schema without mutating its input.
rules.currentBehavior: Schemas 1 through 8 are validated and migrated to schema 9; a failed migration publishes no partial project.

rules.requiredOutcome: The current raw project schema validates, clones, and routes as editable at the core load and migration boundary.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 is the maintained writable raw-project schema and is cloned at the load boundary; this rule does not claim feature-requirement handling at the portable-archive or controller boundary.

rules.requiredOutcome: A bounded pathless main-owned service validates the maintained exact-current-schema project domain before host staging and catalog publication and before returning a shared read document; the renderer repeats validation as defense in depth, without receiving filesystem paths, catalog entry IDs, or lease capabilities. Main-owned startup reclamation preserves every current or recoverable catalog reference, retires abandoned registered stage attempts without removing live writer state, and makes fair progress across a shared bounded budget.
rules.currentBehavior: A fresh filesystem library scope v2 ignores rather than migrates the prior shared v1 scope; a schema 3 database at the v2 path rejects schemas 1 and 2 instead of implicitly migrating, adopting, or backfilling them. Metadata schema 2 binds a separate opaque library entry ID to the bounded project identity, exact schema 9, project revision, byte length, SHA-256 digest, and derived immutable revision-and-digest path. The main-only store canonicalizes the document with the bounded tagged-binary Scape codec, enforces the non-raiseable 256 MiB document ceiling, validates root schema, identity, title, and revision, and reserves its canonical path plus one unique random attempt in lease- and fencing-token-bound authoritative project and stage inventories in the same immediate transaction before exclusive stage creation. When exact-lease cleanup is acknowledged, an exclusive-open failure retires only the registration without unlinking the path, while an error after exclusive creation targets that registered random stage for removal. Lost-lease or failed cleanup leaves the registration for takeover. Successful materialization requires the exact metadata and stage paths, lease ID, and fencing token, then atomically renames and syncs the file, marks the canonical row materialized, removes the stage row, verifies the immutable file against the catalog descriptor, and requires every catalog reference to have a materialized row before publishing an exact +1 catalog revision through the fenced metadata journal. The main-owned identity service applies the shared strict exact-V9 maintained-persistence-domain validator before permitting host staging or catalog publication of a renderer commit; it validates the loaded commit result and a stored project again before returning either canonical document. Every serialized project receives a raw-JSON structural preflight capped at 101,536 JSON values and depth 130 before JSON.parse; each exact-V9 decoded codec traversal and maintained-domain validation phase is independently capped at 100,000 nodes and depth 128. The service threads these lower-only caps through renderer input, loaded commit results, stored reads, and response serialization. Renderer input refusal precedes host mutation or staging; an over-budget loaded commit result is refused before the renderer response, although host publication may already have completed. Future-schema tag-shaped data is structurally counted but is neither decoded nor interpreted. Canonical JSON-derived graphs and ordinary direct objects reject accessors, toJSON hooks, method-shadowed arrays, hidden or symbol data, cycles, exotic containers, and non-JSON scalars without invoking application accessors; hostile proxies and prototype-polluted or exotic injected graphs remain outside that code-safety claim. Counters reset between the lexical, codec, validator, and serialization phases, so these per-phase shape ceilings are not an aggregate work, CPU or elapsed-time, allocation-amplification, cancellation, or resident-memory budget. The validator strictly checks core project, document, media, and graph structures without loading legacy migrations or executable effect and worker runtimes. All audio effects must be cloneable and have the generic effect identity, enabled, and parameter structure; type-specific semantic checks currently cover missing-effect compatibility metadata and parametric EQ, while other first- and third-party effect payload semantics are intentionally not gated yet. The host serializes commits and renews its lease while draining admitted work. After journal recovery and before host exposure, main-only startup maintenance walks the authoritative project and stage inventories by monotonic row IDs, captures independent cycle high-waters, persists both cursors plus an alternating schedule, and scans at most 100,000 total rows per invocation in at-most-64-row batches under immediate SQLite writer fences with exact lease checks before and after filesystem work. A current exact-lease stage remains live; a stale registered regular stage is removed; a missing attempt retires; and a non-regular target or non-direct parent remains untouched and inventoried. Canonical rows owned by the current lease or referenced by an outstanding stage remain ineligible. Stage-cycle completion persists and consumes a canonical rescan flag atomically so retired attempts cannot leave already-scanned parents behind. Canonical batches rebuild portable case-folded reachability from the current catalog plus both sides of any pending recovery journal before moving an unreachable registered canonical regular immutable file through a deterministic noncatalogable quarantine. Unregistered stage-looking, canonical, forged quarantine, and foreign files do not consume inventory budget and remain untouched. A real 100,001-row fixture proves successive bounded passes reach the suffix; later inserts wait for the next high-water cycle; and low- and mixed-cap stage fixtures prove persisted alternation and canonical rescanning. The collector yields between batches, safely retries crash-left quarantine files, fails closed on a static symlinked project root or corrupt metadata, and leaves malformed names, non-regular or symlink entries, and managed-media content untouched. Its identity service and owner-scoped IPC expose only bounded project summaries, canonical documents and bundles, identities, delete results, and managed-source descriptors and chunks for canonical PCM and retained original video; main strips catalog internals and admits at most four active uploads and four active reads across the bridge service, while owner revocation fences new work, aborts owned uploads, and drains admitted operations. The renderer repository repeats the same maintained-persistence-domain exact-V9 validation as defense in depth before local mutation, keeps revision and source/media data in a product-local shadow, treats the shared latest document and summary list as authoritative, and fails closed on an incomplete desktop bridge. A composed source-free editor fixture creates and autosaves in Soundscaper, closes the fenced host, discovers and bootstrap-reopens the same identity and revision from a fresh Framescaper-local store, and commits the next revision in Framescaper while the shared media catalog remains empty. A maintained dedicated Linux x64 CI job builds two separate unpacked packages and runs sequential Soundscaper to Framescaper to Soundscaper processes. They share only one isolated appData root, use separate product profiles, and the final process reuses the Soundscaper profile. Each process waits until the renderer is ready, drives the bounded pathless preload IPC, exact-SHA-256 verifies the expected canonical source-free schema 9 document, commits revisions 1, 2, and 3, checks the renderer summary and main-only catalog row, requires clean recovery, no stale takeover, strictly higher fencing tokens, increasing catalog revisions, and the expected preferred product, and awaits process exit and lease release before continuing. Combined with the composed editor fixture, this closes only the generic packaged source-free preload/IPC/multi-process/executable lifecycle gap. It does not qualify packaged controller autosave or tab activation; source-bearing bytes, playback, or managed media; concurrent opens; crash or stale takeover; interruption or power loss; parent-, database-, or project-root path identity; installers or file associations; or Windows, macOS, or ARM64. Activation-specific feature-capability evaluation and rendered-fallback byte verification remain editor-owned. Third-party activation gating is deliberately outside this slice. Legacy Soundscaper library migration is also deliberately outside this slice. Unregistered or legacy pre-inventory stage-looking files remain foreign and are not adopted or deleted. Migration from the prior shared v1 scope or product-private Soundscaper libraries is intentionally not a current priority and remains deferred and unsupported by this current-only contract; Audacity project import compatibility is a separate boundary.

rules.requiredOutcome: An explicit post-flush handoff of a maintained exact-current-schema desktop project may publish and acquire bounded canonical PCM and retained original-video bodies through pathless IPC. Sender and fresh-recipient admission must reject complete aggregate logical-source, canonical-byte, and PCM-chunk budgets before any source-body read, bridge body transfer, or recipient write. Each absent shared-library binding must admit its prospective catalog row and metadata plus aggregate in-process declared bytes and destination filesystem capacity before hard-link, staging, or body work; publication must stay bound to the main-derived exact catalog project revision and canonical document SHA-256; recipient acquisition must verify identity, kind, storage key, exact byte length and digest plus canonical audio byte geometry before atomic if-absent publication and roll back only records and payload tokens it owns; and same-kind, same-content return handoff may retain a distinct revision-bound descriptor while reusing one verified immutable body, with bounded upload fallback when safe hard-link reuse is unavailable. Main must register exact canonical and stage ownership before filesystem body work, bind catalog publication to materialized inventory, and perform lease-fenced bounded startup retirement and reclamation without adopting unregistered files.
rules.currentBehavior: Ordinary shared-project saves remain document-only. Explicit sender handoff collects at most 4,094 reachable logical sources, deduplicates compatible same-kind physical bindings, rejects conflicting geometry, and preflights one aggregate 64 GiB expanded-byte budget across canonical audio archive bytes and retained original-video bodies plus the 65,536-PCM-chunk ceiling before the first source-body read or bridge body transfer. Each canonical PCM source receives two full digesting reads. Each retained original video requires trusted exact-size SHA-256 metadata and receives two full body-digest passes through at-most-4-MiB windows with metadata revalidation; when a binding is absent, the second audio or video pass also streams at-most-4-MiB pathless chunks. Main permits at most four active uploads and four active reads across the bridge service, with upload sessions owner-bound for authorization and revocation. It loads the exact catalog project, validates reachable source kind, identity, and geometry, derives rather than accepts from the renderer the catalog document SHA-256, and binds managed identity to encoding, project ID, exact revision, exact document digest, and storage-key/media geometry. The serialized host repeats exact revision and document-digest checks before publication, so an older revision or same-revision document variant is neither advertised nor accepted as present. Exact-present reuse requires matching byte length and SHA-256 and reverifies the body; a new regular upload is digest-verified, synced, and atomically renamed before catalog publication. When the exact current binding is absent, main, not the renderer, selects only canonical same-kind catalog donors matching byte length and SHA-256. It fully verifies each donor, creates a random same-directory hard-link stage, verifies the linked body, promotes it without overwriting a winning target, syncs cleanup and directory state, and only then publishes a distinct revision-bound descriptor. Unsupported linking, missing or corrupt donors, and exhausted link counts use the normal bounded upload fallback; operational or access failures fail closed. No renderer path or donor selector is accepted. Each absent audio or video binding synchronously reserves its prospective catalog row and metadata bytes together with other in-flight reservations, enforcing the 50,000-row and 4 MiB metadata ceilings plus a lower-only 64 GiB aggregate declared body-byte ceiling before the filesystem query, hard-link attempt, directory or stage creation, or body consumption. A BigInt statfs of the managed-media destination checks available blocks against aggregate in-flight declared bytes. The reservation remains held until descriptor publication settles and is released idempotently after success, failure and cancellation; publication revalidates the prospective row and metadata against the current catalog. An exact-present retry bypasses a new reservation and statfs, consumes no offered body, and still reverifies the existing body. After point-in-time capacity admission, and before directory or stage creation, hard-link work, or body consumption, main commits an exact canonical row and random upload or reuse stage to schema-3 authoritative inventory with descriptor provenance and the live lease and fencing token. Promotion accepts only the registered regular stage, atomically renames and directory-syncs it, advances the canonical row to materialized, and removes the stage row under persisted before-and-after lease checks. Catalog preparation requires every recognized managed descriptor to have an exact materialized or published row, and catalog commit marks it published atomically with metadata. A body left materialized by catalog failure is reverified and published on exact retry without consuming another offered stream. After metadata-journal recovery and project-file reclamation, startup logically retires only tracked catalog descriptors whose project ID, revision, and document digest are no longer current while preserving unmanaged rows, settles retirement through the normal journal, then alternates persisted stage and canonical high-water batches. At most 100,000 rows are scanned per startup in at-most-64-row lease-fenced transactions. Stale registered regular stages and eligible canonical bodies are removed through exact paths and deterministic quarantine; missing crash states retire; current catalog rows are protected; non-regular, symlinked, unregistered, legacy, and foreign paths remain untouched. Retirement and stage cleanup restart the canonical cursor when eligibility changes. Snapshot counts expose bounded completion, and a startup failure releases the lease. Fresh-recipient acquisition repeats the complete preflight before body reads or recipient writes, installs audio through a staged source writer and video through an owned media-asset writer, and performs exact bounded reads that verify descriptor identity, kind and storage key, byte length, SHA-256, and canonical audio byte geometry before atomic if-absent publication; retained original video stays opaque and is not decoded or probed for media geometry at this boundary. A losing absence race removes only its own staging. Partial acquisition or later pre-shadow failure rolls back in reverse order only the exact acquisition-owned audio record or owned video publication and its source-token, path, or media-chunk payload, preserving a concurrent replacement. Cancellation first observed after the exact authoritative shadow is durable retains that shadow and its acquired managed media while preventing activation. The composed headless Soundscaper-to-fresh-Framescaper-to-Soundscaper fixture proves an empty missing-source set, exact audio engine buffers and video blob URL bytes, transport play, edit and save, same-inode canonical PCM and original-video bodies under distinct revision-bound bindings without renderer body chunks, and return through the original Soundscaper profile with the exact returned document, product-local revision history, zero bridge body I/O, and no duplicate local media. A narrower composed fixture proves that explicit handoff publishes canonical original PCM plus an exact-schema-9 first-party audio whole-mix fallback referenced only by its feature requirement, a fresh Framescaper acquires both absent bodies and the exact canonical shadow, and its read-only controller activates the transient fallback with exact samples. Transfer acquisition verifies the managed descriptor and body SHA-256; the distinct feature-manifest fallback digest remains controller-owned after shadow publication and before activation. It does not qualify packaged executable or UI handoff, browser codec playback, unmanaged or linked originals, authored proxies, generic or video rendered fallbacks, relink or watch behavior, general copy or consolidation, continuous runtime cleanup beyond the startup-bounded tracked inventory; whole-handoff or durable capacity reservation; operating-system reservation, exact allocation or write-time capacity; allocation-unit rounding, SQLite or WAL overhead; external writers or separate store instances or processes; portable hard-link capacity behavior; durable playback identity; or a shared cross-product revision journal or undo/redo history.

rules.requiredOutcome: An authoritative latest exact-schema-9 desktop shared-project load with reachable source references must preflight its complete logical-source, canonical-byte, and PCM-chunk budgets before any source-body read, shared body transfer, or recipient write; acquire exact managed canonical PCM and retained original video into a fresh recipient through digest-verified atomic if-absent publication where available; qualify every remaining source through bounded recipient-local admission; and fail before activation without deleting a concurrent local replacement.
rules.currentBehavior: The renderer collects at most 4,094 reachable timeline, Project Bin, and fallback source references. Compatible same-kind physical bindings are deduplicated and conflicting geometry rejects. One aggregate 64 GiB expanded-byte budget charges canonical audio archive bytes plus recipient-local and managed original-video bodies, while a 65,536-PCM-chunk budget charges audio. Both budgets are completed before any source-body read, shared body transfer, or recipient write. A fresh recipient acquires matching managed canonical-PCM and original-video descriptors through bounded 4 MiB reads: audio uses a staged source writer and video uses an owned media-asset writer. It verifies logical identity, kind and storage key, exact byte length, SHA-256, and canonical audio byte geometry, then atomically publishes only if the storage key remains absent; retained original video stays opaque and is not decoded or probed for media geometry at this boundary. A losing absence race removes only the writer's staging and preserves the winner. Partial transfer, conflicting binding, or later pre-shadow failure rolls back in reverse order by conditionally deleting only the exact acquisition-owned audio record or owned video publication and its source-token, path, or media-chunk payload; a concurrent replacement remains current and intact. Once the exact authoritative shadow is durable, acquisition is committed, so late cancellation rejects before activation but retains the shadow and managed PCM and original video it references. Every source not trusted through managed acquisition still requires the pre-existing latest recipient-local exact-schema-9 snapshot of the same project to bind logical source identity, kind, storage key, MIME type, frame and sample geometry, and kind-specific media descriptor. Compatible aliases are verified once; conflicting bindings reject. Unmanaged audio consumes ordered Float32Array PCM with exact chunk, channel, and frame geometry; video requires a trusted recipient-local SHA-256 before a full exact-size Blob read and hash through 4 MiB windows. Legacy PCM-on-read migration and media-digest backfill remain disabled. Pre-shadow source integrity, availability, binding, geometry, budget, body, and digest failures preserve the prior local shadow and history and prevent activation. Source-free loads perform no media I/O; one repository instance serializes latest load, save, and delete per project. Maintained evidence includes already-present mixed audio/video admission, missing-PCM refusal, fresh managed mixed-media acquisition, the composed headless Soundscaper-to-Framescaper-to-Soundscaper return, and a first-party audio whole-mix fallback referenced only by its exact-schema-9 manifest, acquired with canonical original PCM into a fresh recipient before separate controller digest verification and activation. Managed transfer verifies its descriptor and body digest, not the project fallback declaration. Managed mixed-media acquisition does not turn unmanaged admission into an atomic snapshot or publisher-authenticated stable playback lease. Linked and unmanaged originals, authored proxies, generic or video rendered fallbacks, relink, watch behavior, general copy or consolidation, shared managed-media runtime cleanup beyond the startup-bounded tracked inventory, recipient-local or whole-handoff capacity reservation, stable playback identity, packaged executable and UI handoff, browser codec playback, portable hard-link qualification, and shared cross-product revision and undo history remain unqualified. Existing V1-V8 raw-project migrations remain maintained; prior shared-v1 and product-private-library migration stays deferred and unsupported, while Audacity import remains separate. Other first- and third-party effect semantics remain intentionally not gated.

rules.requiredOutcome: Disposable poster and thumbnail derivatives must bind a trusted retained original and its content digest to the derivative type, time, versioned recipe, and output integrity. They remain reproducible cache state outside project history, .scape media, and managed handoff, while authored rendered fallback state and media remain durable.
rules.currentBehavior: The derivative repository derives the current original storage identity, trusted SHA-256, and local generation token instead of accepting provenance from its caller. A content-addressed relationship binds the original storage key and digest, poster or thumbnail type, normalized timestamp, recipe ID, and recipe version. Publication canonicalizes and hashes the output, then revalidates the original immediately before memory publication or in the same IndexedDB transaction as the payload and scalar companion. Loads resolve against the current original, require the payload and companion relationship fields to agree, verify exact output size and SHA-256, and treat unbound legacy rows or a replaced original generation as a cache miss. Maintained recipe revisions coexist under distinct identities; default lookup selects only the maintained revision. New video imports use null preview locators, maintained read-write .scape imports null legacy locator values, maintained source-update commands cannot author them, desktop recipient binding ignores them, and managed source declarations omit them. The project schema continues to accept those nullable fields so old and future documents remain parseable, but maintained playback resolves previews from the trusted original relationship rather than durable locator identity. Derivative cache records and bodies are not project-history roots, portable archive assets, or managed-media transfers; archive export includes only the canonical source assets in its manifest and ZIP inventory. Rendered fallback descriptors and their referenced sources remain durable project and archive state under their separate compatibility rules. The maintained exact-schema first-party audio whole-mix fallback is separately qualified for fresh-recipient managed acquisition and activation; generic and video fallbacks remain unqualified. These disposable previews are not editorial proxies and do not provide relink, watch, freeze, export, decoder-memory, or cross-product proxy behavior.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current raw project documents carry a bounded normalized declarative feature-requirements manifest, retained-schema migrations do not invent publisher declarations, maintained exact-current-schema create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile editor-owned first-party declarations from project state, and pure evaluation classifies caller-declared availability without activating project data.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 validates and deep-clones manifest schema 1, canonical feature identifiers, unique requirement IDs, closed dispositions, bounded collections and strings, and rendered-fallback descriptor source kind and digest syntax. Exact-schema-9 create, load, clone, and commit reconcile the reserved soundscaper.audio-effects bypass requirement when a maintained first-party processor exists in a non-label or non-video track, mixer group, mixer send, or master rack, and the reserved soundscaper.video-effects bypass requirement when a maintained first-party video effect exists on a timeline or Project Bin video clip. Disabled effects and inactive audio racks still declare preservation; missing or foreign effect types and video-effect stacks on non-video clips do not. An explicit publisher declaration for the same capability wins without duplication, and conflicting use of either reserved requirement ID rejects. V1-V8 migration starts from an empty publisher manifest and applies the same owned reconciliation. Evaluation reports available, unavailable, and unknown requirements while retaining the declared bypass or rendered-fallback disposition separately from the native, bypassed, or rendered-fallback effective disposition without mutating the manifest.

rules.requiredOutcome: A current-schema portable archive retains the normalized feature-requirements manifest and every fallback-only source asset, including consistent known source-reference rewriting on copy collisions.
rules.currentBehavior: Schema 9 rendered-fallback descriptors root source metadata during project and history compaction. Current-format .scape export serializes the manifest and every project source asset, import preserves the manifest and its evaluation semantics, and copy import rewrites known fallback source IDs through the same collision map as source identity. Digest integrity is governed by the route-specific current-scape-rendered-fallback-integrity rule; arbitrary future schemas remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current-format, exact-current-schema .scape routes bind every rendered fallback claim to its canonical archive asset and reject a kind or digest mismatch before publication.
rules.currentBehavior: Export snapshots the admitted project root and complete source records before asynchronous asset work and serializes the same source snapshots and bounded normalized fallback manifest used for validation. Project-root and source-record accessors and callable toJSON hooks are rejected without invocation so they cannot rewrite the admitted serialization; export then hashes every emitted source body and rejects a mismatch against the completed descriptors before manifest write or destination commit. Import and inspection bind each exact-schema-9 fallback source ID, kind, and SHA-256 to the canonical manifest asset before collision lookup or storage; import then verifies the extracted asset body size and SHA-256 before source or project publication. Inspection performs descriptor binding only and does not read or hash asset bodies. Copy import rewrites the source ID while preserving the verified digest. Future schemas return and featureRequirements is not traversed. Raw-project and stored-project loads plus runtime fallback use remain outside this route-specific integrity rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: Maintained current-schema projects are evaluated against a stable selected-product capability registry before activation, and every unavailable or unregistered requirement makes the document intrinsically read-only with a per-tab compatibility report.
rules.currentBehavior: Explicit stable broad org.soundscaper.capability feature IDs map one-to-one to the capability keys in both maintained product profiles. Only a strict true profile value is available; registered non-true capabilities are unavailable and unregistered feature IDs are unknown. The controller evaluates exact schema 9 from the actual project history that will be activated before activation side effects and makes every report containing an unavailable or unknown requirement intrinsically read-only. When an existing same-ID tab wins, its stored read-only declaration also wins over the ignored incoming document's flags. The report is retained per tab, remains deeply frozen across session metadata clones, and is exposed on the document snapshot. Future schemas return no report and featureRequirements is not traversed. A separate controller-admission rule verifies declared fallback bytes; runtime fallback use remains outside this report rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: An activated exact-current-schema document with an incompatible feature report keeps a persistent structured notice associated with the active tab without activating project data or offering a compatibility override.
rules.currentBehavior: The maintained workspace consumes the active document snapshot's deeply frozen featureRequirementsCompatibility report directly. When compatible is false, it derives a separate frozen notice from only unavailable and unknown items, recomputes their counts, and persistently displays a non-dismissible localized document-level region with bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and the declared bypass or rendered-fallback disposition whenever that project tab is active. The effective disposition remains available as structured metadata rather than being mislabeled as the declaration. Available items are excluded; evaluator messages and fallback internals are not read or rendered; and the notice exposes no activation controls or generic rendered-fallback substitution or third-party-loading claim; the exact first-party audio active-playback indicator is bound by its separate rule. Switching to a compatible or null-report tab removes the notice, and switching back restores it from that active tab's report. Future schemas produce a null report, and the workspace does not inspect their featureRequirements value. Outside the separate first-party audio- and video-effect rules, this document-level notice is not a generic affected-object placeholder, per-feature bypass control, runtime fallback selection, future-schema guarantee, or third-party activation gate.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, unavailable maintained first-party audio rack effects declared for bypass reach the editor engine only through a bounded non-persisted bypass projection while canonical state remains unchanged and every affected object stays visibly identified on its active tab.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains a registered audioEffects item that is unavailable, declares bypass, and has the effective bypassed disposition. Active, enabled, not-already-bypassed maintained processors in non-label and non-video track, mixer-group, mixer-send, and master racks become minimal bypassed engine copies; inactive racks, disabled or already-bypassed effects, and missing or foreign effect types remain untouched. Stable IDs and effect types are bounded, the lower-only production ceiling is 4,096 affected effects, overflow rejects instead of truncating, and placeholder metadata never reads or retains effect params, context, state, or other payloads. Only engine loading receives the projection: the canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, and save paths remain unchanged. Projection metadata is deeply frozen across per-tab session clones and the document snapshot. The active compatibility notice matches that metadata to one qualifying requirement and renders localized control-free affected-effect placeholders with maintained effect labels and canonical track, group, send, or master ownership without reading effect payloads. Future schemas return unchanged before rack traversal. This rule does not cover unknown or third-party effects, rendered-fallback substitution, offline render or export, per-feature activation controls, or arbitrary future schemas.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, one unavailable registered first-party audioEffects requirement declared for rendered fallback replaces canonical audio paths with its admitted mono or stereo whole-mix only for editor playback while canonical state remains unchanged and activation stays visibly identified. Explicit managed desktop handoff must retain a fallback source referenced only by that requirement through fresh-recipient acquisition, controller digest verification, and activation.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains exactly one registered audioEffects item that is unavailable with declared and effective rendered-fallback dispositions, and the report descriptor exactly matches the canonical manifest requirement. One referenced audio source must be mono or stereo, use its full safe frame range from frame zero, and match the project sample rate and master channel count; ADM and surround projects reject, as do ambiguous candidates, missing or mismatched sources, and unsafe geometry, while reserved synthetic track or clip ID collisions also reject. The transient projection removes canonical audio clips and tracks, installs one neutral whole-mix clip and track, neutralizes mixer and master processing, and retains video and label timing. The shared playback project service applies the same projection during initial activation and later engine reapplies. Required stored metadata is rechecked; short sources are decoded and their buffer geometry must match exactly, while oversized sources must expose a streamable chunk provider. Readiness does not prefetch or revalidate streamed chunks, so later provider failure remains possible. Initial activation stages only the required fallback source's decoded buffer or stream-provider candidate privately before acquiring the session activation reservation, without mutating shared source-buffer or provider state or publishing engine chunk sources. Metadata, audio-context, and decoded-body operations race the controller-lifetime signal, reject cancellation promptly with its exact reason, and fence late settlement from publishing buffers, chunk providers, engine chunk sources, missing-source state, or status. If post-preparation currentness or reservation fails, the candidate is discarded and the prior buffer and provider identities, engine chunk-source state, active project, tab, and lock remain unchanged. After currentness and reservation succeed, ordinary-source loading excludes the required fallback. Ordinary transient buffers and the staged required representation are composed into private source-buffer and chunk-source snapshots; the staged required representation wins a conflicting transient before those snapshots reach the engine. After the engine callback succeeds and the lifetime signal remains active, commit runs its caller-supplied synchronous project-identity or activation-admission assertion immediately before shared publication, with no intervening await; only then do the shared source maps change. Each canonical playback reapply owns one replaceable controller-lifetime task. A newer reapply or a successful project switch aborts stalled metadata, audio-context, and decoded-body source preparation with the exact reason and fences late settlement from buffers, chunk providers, engine chunk sources, missing-source state, or status. In the tested stalled-preparation race, only the newest source-ready projection enters the engine. Explicit desktop handoff roots a qualifying fallback-only source through the manifest, publishes it as canonical managed PCM alongside the editable original, and lets a fresh recipient acquire both bodies plus the exact canonical shadow. Transfer acquisition authenticates the managed descriptor and body SHA-256, while the controller separately verifies the manifest fallback digest after shadow publication and before sending the transient whole-mix projection and exact fallback samples to the engine. The canonical project, history, persistence, save, export, and offline render paths remain unchanged. Deeply frozen per-tab and document-snapshot metadata drives one persistent localized active during editor playback indicator without exposing the source ID or digest. Controller digest admission is point-in-time and is not a durable byte lease. An engine apply already entered is not abortable or transactional and can leave engine-side effects after callback failure or cancellation. A later activation failure after a successful commit does not roll back committed shared source state or earlier activation effects. Ordinary-source loading remains outside this required-source staging transaction. Short-buffer retention after engine application remains subject to cache-fit policy. Streamed chunks are not prefetched or revalidated after readiness. Generic or video fallback, ADM or surround playback, freeze and proxy authoring, unknown or third-party activation, future schemas, and earlier Soundscaper schemas remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: On maintained exact-current-schema activation, unavailable maintained first-party video effects declared for bypass reach editor playback only through a bounded non-persisted bypass projection while canonical state remains unchanged and every affected timeline or Project Bin effect stays visibly identified on its active tab.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller evaluates the authoritative actual project history and projects only exact schema 9 when its soundscaper-project report contains a registered videoEffects item that is unavailable, declares bypass, and has the effective bypassed disposition. Enabled maintained effects on timeline and Project Bin video clips become minimal disabled activation copies; disabled effects and missing, foreign, or wrong-kind stacks remain untouched. Stable clip and effect IDs are bounded to 256 characters, effect types to 128 characters, the lower-only production ceiling is 4,096 affected effects across both locations, and overflow rejects instead of truncating. Each placeholder entry records only location, clip ID, effect ID, and effect type without reading or retaining params, context, state, or other opaque payloads. Only transient engine loading receives the project projection, and the WebGL preview filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks using trusted metadata while caching selectors and preserving unchanged stack references. The canonical project, history, source loading, persistence, save, and export or offline-render paths remain unchanged. Projection metadata is deeply frozen across per-tab session clones and the document snapshot. The active compatibility notice matches that metadata to one qualifying requirement and renders localized control-free affected-effect placeholders with maintained effect labels and canonical Timeline or Project Bin clip ownership without reading effect payloads. Future schemas return unchanged before clip or Project Bin traversal. This rule does not cover unknown or third-party effects, rendered-fallback substitution, export or offline render behavior, per-feature activation controls, arbitrary future schemas, or earlier Soundscaper project schemas.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every rendered fallback referenced by an exact-current-schema raw or stored project admitted through the maintained controller is verified against its canonical local stored bytes before activation side effects.
rules.currentBehavior: The controller verifies the authoritative exact-schema-9 activation project, including existing same-ID tab history bound by a session-owned history token. After verification it obtains one exclusive session activation reservation before project-generation invalidation, recording or engine shutdown, lock changes, ordinary engine-source loading, or normal activation persistence. The reservation rejects target history replacement, close/reopen, and competing active-project publication through synchronous session publication and is released in finally. Admission reads disable on-access PCM migration scheduling and retained-media digest claim/backfill, so verification does not publish storage maintenance. Audio claims hash the canonical audio-f32le-chunks-v1 sequence through the same checked PCM geometry and cumulative 65,536-chunk ceiling as .scape export. Video claims hash a genuine immutable original-media Blob body incrementally through the non-raiseable 4 MiB media-digest window. Unique claimed audio bytes and admitted video sizes share a non-raiseable 64 GiB cumulative ceiling before fallback body reads. Verification is sequential and cooperatively cancellable through the maintained store. Read-only video-metadata preflight is raced against cancellation, so an injected signal-ignoring provider may continue after admission rejects; a provider-stalled fallback body read can instead delay cancellation settlement and iterator cleanup. Verification deduplicates identical source claims, rejects conflicting digests before storage reads, and rejects missing, malformed, or mismatched local assets. Empty manifests and future schemas perform no asset reads, and future featureRequirements are not traversed. This admission-time rule does not verify arbitrary direct store.loadProject calls, continuously bind against later low-level source replacement, establish publisher authenticity, substitute fallback media at runtime, or provide a complete third-party activation gate.

rules.requiredOutcome: Current-format portable archive inspection evaluates maintained project feature requirements against the selected product before collision lookup, import, persistence, or activation without interpreting future project schemas.
rules.currentBehavior: The selected product is snapshotted through the shared compatibility service and injected into inspection as a provider-owned option after caller options, so a caller cannot override it. After current-format archive integrity, project-source validation, and rendered-fallback claim-to-descriptor binding, exact schema 9 is evaluated before project collision lookup and returned as a deeply frozen featureRequirementsCompatibility report. Inspection does not hash asset bodies. Future project schemas return null and featureRequirements is not traversed. This programmatic surface is the foundation for the maintained open decision; it does not use fallbacks at runtime or gate third-party activation.

rules.requiredOutcome: Every current-format, exact-current-schema archive opened through the maintained workspace/UI file routes with an incompatible selected-product feature report requires explicit compatibility-bearing consent or cancellation before import, persistence, or activation, in both collision and no-collision flows.
rules.currentBehavior: Maintained workspace/UI file-open routes use one replaceable owned request from inspection through a closed decision. A no-collision incompatible report permits only open-read-only or cancel; a combined incompatibility and ID collision permits only copy-read-only or cancel in one decision; compatible collisions permit only copy or cancel. Distinct compatibility-bearing choices fail closed against stale collision callbacks. Cancel resolves before native import, persistence, or activation. The localized dialog exposes bounded display names, stable feature IDs, availability, and declared disposition without claiming fallback verification or runtime use; incompatible decisions default focus to Cancel and support Escape dismissal and focus restoration. Acceptance passes only the existing copy collision policy into native open, after which the controller reevaluates the actual project history and enforces it as intrinsically read-only. Future-schema null reports skip this decision. The low-level native-open API retains its caller-supplied collision policy, and it and third-party activation remain outside this rule.

rules.requiredOutcome: A raw project document with a newer schema is cloned without normalization and cannot enter a mutation or overwrite path.
rules.currentBehavior: The core migration boundary returns newer objects as structured clones with readOnly=true and reason=newer-schema.

rules.requiredOutcome: A future-schema portable archive opens read-only and can be exported unchanged without ID, storage-key, binary, or unknown-field loss.
rules.currentBehavior: The archive importer traverses known collections and may rewrite project and source identity, so arbitrary future-schema .scape round trips are not yet claimed.

rules.requiredOutcome: Designated JSON opaque extension fields survive migration, clone, save, and portable archive reopen semantically unchanged.
rules.currentBehavior: Legacy unknown JSON fields are collected under opaqueExtensions.legacyV1 and JSON-compatible opaqueExtensions survive current-schema .scape round trips.

rules.requiredOutcome: Supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque state in exact-current-schema, current-format .scape projects uses a tagged, bounded JSON encoding and round-trips byte-exactly without activation.
rules.currentBehavior: Before JSON.parse, every schema receives an iterative raw-JSON structural preflight bounded to 101,536 values and depth 130 in production; the descriptor allowance preserves round-trip closure for the bounded tagged representation. Exact schema 9 export encodes Uint8Array values, offset-view bytes, and ArrayBuffer values with a reserved tagged descriptor; export and post-parse decode independently enforce the lower-only logical limits of 100,000 traversal nodes and depth 128, while other ArrayBuffer views reject. The binary budget also admits at most 256 payloads, 4 MiB per payload, and 8 MiB aggregate bytes. Import and inspection validate the closed descriptor schema, unique positive IDs, canonical base64, exact byte lengths, and all limits before allocating decoded payloads, then restore the declared binary type without interpreting its bytes. Reserved-tag collisions, project-container accessors, and callable container toJSON hooks reject without invocation. Future-schema tag-shaped data is structurally counted by the raw preflight but is neither decoded nor interpreted as a binary descriptor.

rules.requiredOutcome: Unavailable native features remain visible and bypassable, retain editable opaque state, declare requirements, and reference an audible or visible fallback when available.
rules.currentBehavior: The schema 9 manifest, evaluator, retention roots, current-format .scape paths, selected-product controller report, and current-format .scape inspection report preserve and classify declared requirements. Maintained exact-schema-9 create, load, clone, and commit paths reconcile the owned first-party audio- and video-effects requirements. The bounded first-party audio-effect slice loads qualifying unavailable rack processors through a transient engine bypass projection, and the bounded first-party video-effect slice loads minimal disabled activation copies and filters exact affected effects from timeline stacks in WebGL preview; persistent localized control-free affected-object placeholders follow the active tab for both slices. A separate exact-schema-9 first-party audio whole-mix rendered-fallback slice substitutes one admitted mono or stereo source only for editor playback while canonical state remains unchanged and the active tab identifies that fallback use. Maintained opens provide an actionable pre-open read-only or cancel decision, the broader persistent document-level post-open report follows the active tab, and the controller still makes an activated project with an unavailable or unknown requirement intrinsically read-only. Current-format exact-schema .scape archive fallback integrity verifies the declared digest against the canonical asset, while inspection performs pre-collision descriptor binding without reading asset bodies. Maintained exact-schema-9 controller activation also verifies referenced local audio and video fallback bytes before activation side effects. The bounded current-schema .scape codec preserves supported Uint8Array and ArrayBuffer opaque native/effect state byte-exactly without activation; other buffer views remain unsupported. Generic per-object placeholders and per-feature bypass controls beyond these maintained first-party audio- and video-effect slices, rendered-fallback runtime use beyond the first-party audio whole-mix playback slice, and arbitrary future-schema archive preservation are not implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: Video originals and reproducible proxies retain an explicit relationship, and proxy use never changes editorial time or original delivery semantics.
rules.currentBehavior: Video source originals are retained, but the roadmap proxy relationship and offline/relink model are not implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: Freeze, unfreeze, commit, and rendered fallback state preserve the editable source and native-effect metadata.
rules.currentBehavior: Offline rendering and the narrow exact-schema-9 playback fallback exist, but no canonical authored freeze, unfreeze, commit, relink, or rendered-fallback document state and no generic cross-platform fallback-authoring contract are implemented.

rules.requiredOutcome: An unknown .scape container format is rejected before project or media persistence rather than guessed or partially imported.
rules.currentBehavior: The manifest parser accepts only formatVersion 1 and import staging rolls back source writes on failure.
